title: Oven Roasted French Duck Terrine
description: A classic French dish featuring tender duck, clear honey, and a bitter, glassy jelly, perfect for a weeknight dinner. This low-fat-friendly terrine is made with a delicate balance of flavors and textures.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 300 degrees Fahrenheit.
Season the duck breast with black pepper and thyme.
Roast the duck breast in the oven for 20 minutes, or until it reaches an internal temperature of 145 degrees Fahrenheit.
Let the duck breast rest for 10 minutes before slicing it into thin strips.
In a small saucepan, combine the clear honey, port wine, and chicken broth, and bring to a boil over medium heat.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer the mixture for 10 minutes, or until it has reduced by half.
Remove the saucepan from the heat and stir in the gelatin until it is fully dissolved.
Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl, and let it cool to room temperature.
To assemble the terrine, layer the sliced duck breast, shallots, and honey-gelatin mixture in a terrine mold, repeating the layers two or three times.
Refrigerate the terrine for at least 2 hours, or until it is set.
To serve, remove the terrine from the refrigerator and let it sit at room temperature for 30 minutes, then slice it into thick slices and serve.
